english: The sun was burning and the kind-minded herdsman lay down under the hazel. Sleep seized him and the sheep slipped away. When he woke he did not see them. He feared that enemies would steal them. He searched for them on the mountain and in the water. His dog followed him. The dog tracked the sheep and found them. The kind-minded one drove them into the enclosure. He said: 'I will never sleep under the hazel again.'
uncertain: troméyet + clause rather than ablative object
sésoh₂ read as 1sg subjunctive of ses- 'sleep'

english: Sleep is the brother of death. Sleep comes to men at night. He seizes them and quickly lets them go. Death snatches them and does not let them go. Polh₁uh₁ekwos was asleep in the field. Sleep and Death both came to him. Death said: 'Brother, let us seize him together.' Sleep said: 'Do not seize him; he has endured.' When it dawned, Polh₁uh₁ekwos woke and went away. Death says: 'Later he will come.' He is the giver of goods. Men, praise him; he let you go.
uncertain: h₂wésm̥ after h₁yód - expected h₂wést 'it dawned'
séh₁t 'let go' tense mixed with presents

english: Two daughters trembled at night. They asked: 'Mother, why does night come? We are afraid.' She said: 'My two dear ones, do not fear. Night is the sister of dawn. She clothes the earth, and the sheep lie in sleep. Then Dawn, daughter of the sky, comes forth and they wake. She does not deceive; those who sleep, she will protect them.' Then the two lay down and sleep took them.
uncertain: trésowos read as 'we (two/pl) are afraid' - form unclear (1du?)
tóns masc acc pl for sleepers

english: The king's son, the well-born, (wanted to) see the night. His mother said: 'Lie down.' He did not lie down; he sat on the mountain. He watched the sky and turned about. A beast crept up; the well-born trembled but did not flee. Then it dawned and the sun came forth. He came down and said: 'I have seen night and dawn. She is great, she is dear.' Then sleep took him.

Two brothers were herding cows in the field. When it grew dark they lay down and were asleep. A stranger came by night stealthily and drove them away. When it dawned the two brothers woke. Well-famed said: 'Brother, the cows have left us.' God-born said: 'Let us search for them.' The two tracked them by the water. They saw the stranger asleep near the herd/tired. They drove them home. He did not wake. Sleep took the cows and sleep gave them back. The two vowed afterwards to stand sleepless.

english: Good-horse went to the field and lay down under the hazel. A great sleep took him. He lay in sleep for many nights. Leaves fell and leaves grew again. Then he woke and went home. A man stood at the house. Good-horse did not recognize him and asked: 'Who are you?' He answered: 'I am the son of Good-horse. My father left and perished.' Then he was astonished and said: 'Your father is I.' (The son) rejoiced and seated him at the fire. He said: 'You have come (?) and I was asleep.'
uncertain: h₁eh₁lówdʰth₂e is 2sg perfect but speaker seems to talk of himself - person clash?
